# Annotate (`agy-annotate`)

Use this skill when the user runs `/annotate` or asks to annotate assistant responses, documents, or webpages.

## Execution Guide for the Agent:

### 1. When the user types `/annotate` (or asks to review the last reply):
Run the command:
```bash
npx --yes --package @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest agy-annotate tui
```
This opens the bundled reviewer in an interactive window (via Ghostty or Terminal). When the user finishes adding annotations and presses `q` (or `Ctrl+S`), the window closes, the command outputs the feedback, and you proceed to apply the requested changes.

### 2. When the user specifies a document (e.g., `/annotate path/to/doc.md`):
Run the command:
```bash
npx --yes --package @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest agy-annotate tui "<path/to/doc.md>"
```

### 3. When the user provides a URL/HTML file (e.g., `/annotate page.html`) or asks for webpage review:
Run the command:
```bash
npx --yes --package @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest agy-annotate web [url-or-html-path]
```
Inform the user that the session is paired with Chrome and ready in the Annotate side panel (`Alt+Shift+A`). When the user sends notes from Chrome, they are delivered directly to this session.

# OpenCode Annotate **Review OpenCode AI replies, Markdown documents, and webpages — send annotated feedback to the originating session.** [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate) [![CI](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [Website](https://mjshao.fun/opencode-annotate/) · [Install](#install) · [Workflows](#workflows) · [Browser review](#browser-review-optional) · [Configuration](#configuration) This **unofficial OpenCode plugin** bundles the native [terminal reviewer](tui/README.md) — no separate reviewer install is required. The optional [browser companion](#browser-review-optional) adds Chrome delivery and Safari copy-only review. Published on npm as `@nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate`. | Surface | Reviews | Entry point | |---|---|---| | Terminal (bundled TUI) | AI replies, Markdown, plain text | `/annotate` | | Chrome (optional) | Webpages, local HTML | `/annotate ` or extension | | Safari (optional, copy-only) | Webpages | `/annotate ` or extension | ## Install Requires **OpenCode 2.2.0+**. The npm package includes **Annotate TUI**, built from [`tui/`](tui/README.md) for macOS arm64/x64, Linux arm64/x64 and Windows x64. See its [platform requirements](tui/README.md#source-and-build). The OpenCode terminal handoff has been tested on macOS; Windows handoff has not yet been verified. ```sh opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest ```

The real bundled reviewer, using a synthetic Markdown plan. [Capture details](https://github.com/nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate/blob/main/docs/assets/README.md). OpenCode loads the server tools and TUI commands from one entry in your global **`opencode.json`** or **`opencode.jsonc`**. Run `/reload` if the command list has not refreshed. Manual configuration, preserving other entries: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["@nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest"] } ``` `@latest` selects the current npm release when installing or updating; publishing a release does not itself replace an installed copy. Keep your existing plugin `options`. ## First review in 3 steps 1. **Open the reviewer** — run `/annotate` in any session to review the last completed assistant reply. 2. **Select and comment** — drag to select text (or press `v` and move), then press `c` to comment. Press Enter to save the note. 3. **Send** — press `q` to send your annotations back to the session. The feedback is submitted as a prompt to the originating conversation, resuming it for the assistant to act on. Empty and cancelled reviews submit nothing. Opening a review makes no model call. **`Ctrl+S`** saves the current comment and sends in one step. The header's **Send N back (q)** button does the same as `q`. **`Ctrl+C`** returns without sending, and OpenCode asks whether to send. `E` and `S` send as well, following any `[keys]` rebinding. Confirmed text and browser sends continue the captured session with `steer` / `resume: true`, including while a turn is running. ## Workflows ### Annotate AI responses `/annotate` opens the last completed reply. `/annotate-pick` chooses from recent replies and progress updates. `/annotate-selection` opens the message containing your last transcript selection. Reasoning, tool-call commentary, and in-progress messages are excluded. For a selection that spans messages, `/annotate-selection` reviews just the selected text. ### Review Markdown and text documents ```text /annotate docs/plan.md # Review a Markdown document /annotate "docs/release plan.md" # Path with spaces /annotate ~/Documents/notes.txt # Plain text ``` Local UTF-8 `.md`, `.mdx`, `.markdown` and `.txt` files up to 2 MiB. Relative paths resolve against the captured session's working directory, not the directory from which the terminal client happened to start. Absolute and `~/` paths work too. The file must exist on the machine running the terminal client. The reviewer reads a fixed snapshot and does not edit the original file. Feedback includes the original path and snapshot hash, with instructions to re-read the current file before applying suggestions. Document review works even before the session has an assistant reply. ### Browser webpage feedback Open the extension panel on any webpage and choose an automatically registered OpenCode session. Select text or pick an element, write notes across pages, and send the grouped round to that destination. `/annotate` can also open an explicit browser target: ```text /annotate page.html # Review a local HTML file /annotate https://example.com # Review a webpage ```

# Annotate TUI

The terminal reviewer is an owned component of **OpenCode Annotate**. Source, tests,
builds and releases live in this repository; `tui/` is an ordinary subfolder.

## Source and build

- `src/`: terminal UI, Markdown layout, source mapping, comments, selection and export.
- `schema/`: annotation types and anchor resolution.
- `hosts/`: local transcript readers used by standalone review commands.
- `tests/`: command-line integration tests; unit tests live alongside the Rust modules.
- `binary.mjs`: one package-relative executable resolver shared by OpenCode and AGY.

From the repository root (Rust 1.96+ and Node 22+):

```sh
npm run build:tui
npm run check:tui
node tui/run.mjs --version
node tui/run.mjs document.md
```

Builds land in `tui/bin/<platform>-<arch>/annotate-tui` (`.exe` on Windows). The npm release
contains all supported executables; normal use needs neither Cargo nor another TUI install.
CI builds and tests macOS arm64/x64, Linux x64/arm64 and Windows x64 from these sources.
Linux x64 and arm64 target Ubuntu 22.04/glibc 2.35+.
Windows native tests run in CI; the OpenCode terminal handoff still needs Windows validation.

## Configuration and delivery

User layout and key settings live in `~/.config/opencode-annotate/tui.toml`
(`%APPDATA%/opencode-annotate/tui.toml` on Windows). A comfortable layout:

```toml
[ui]
horizontal_margin = 2
max_width = 168
doc_width = 120
```

`[prompts] what` is the instruction feedback adds once when it contains `what?` notes;
an empty string sends the notes alone. `annotate-tui config` prints the default.

Hosted reviews write their send intent for the adapter: `q` sends notes and returns,
`Ctrl+S` also saves an open comment, and `Ctrl+C` returns to the adapter's confirmation.
The adapters own session targeting and delivery. Markdown labels such as `**题库：**把`
render in bold while selections still map to original source bytes.

The `PLANNOTATOR_*` environment names, internal library identifiers and annotation JSON
keys remain stable so existing retained drafts can be recovered. They do not fetch or
load anything from another project. `PLANNOTATOR_TUI_CONFIG` selects a private per-review
theme copy; the user's file stays intact.

Standalone annotation data defaults to `~/.local/share/opencode-annotate/tui`
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%/opencode-annotate/tui` on Windows). Hosted reviews use their own private
snapshot stores. An explicit `PLANNOTATOR_DATA_DIR` can still open a retained older draft.

# Annotate HTML-derived browser companion

Based on Asim Sayed's MIT-licensed [Annotate HTML](https://github.com/AsimSayed/annotate-html), Chrome Web Store release 1.0.0 (extension ID `ageaediaogfbmbmjoamkcloagepjcgdp`).

`upstream/annotate-1.0.0.js` preserves the unmodified released JavaScript, SHA-256 `ae30233d0db847c21ced822c63ec5f0ead1c6f361518ec28a21ea49defcd1206`; its MIT license is adjacent. Icons are preserved from that release. The original implementation credits Agentation for its element-identification approach.

`inspector.js` adapts the original element identification, computed-style snapshot, and accessibility collectors. This local enhancement replaces the in-page comment popup and volatile state with an extension-origin side panel, durable per-note storage, exact range context and validated selectors. It adds complete export and opt-in paired session delivery. The original upstream implementation is not injected alongside the enhanced runtime.

This is a distinct local extension with its own ID, not an official Annotate HTML update. It has no upstream update URL, analytics or external data service. Only user-requested Native Messaging can send feedback to a paired local OpenCode client.

This version runs in Chrome and Safari. Chrome uses its native messaging host and a docked side panel. Safari has no docked panel, and it only registers an App-Sandboxed app extension, which cannot reach the local Node bridge. The Safari build therefore keeps notes local and copies rounds out, and the panel opens as its own window. Chrome keeps Native Messaging and session delivery. Both browsers are macOS-only in this version.
